question: In accordance with Article 17(3) of the Treaty on European Union, Commissioners must act with complete independence and solely represent the interests of the Union and not those of their Member State of origin.

In the context of the conflict in the Middle East, it has been reported that a Commissioner has adopted a stance or expressed herself in a way that could be understood as supporting the position of the Spanish Government – and thus not as an expression of a common EU position.

To be specific: the Spanish Commissioner has accused Israel of genocide, while the Commissioner responsible for the matter has made it clear that the Commission has no competence whatsoever to judge whether genocide is taking place anywhere.1 1.
What is the Commission’s view on the Spanish Commissioner’s behaviour in the light of the obligation of independence of Commissioners laid down in the EU Treaties?
What are the Commission’s internal procedures and criteria in case a Commissioner violates the requirement for impartiality and loyalty to the EU?
What specific steps has the President of the Commission taken to investigate this matter or, if appropriate, impose disciplinary consequences on the Spanish Commissioner?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.6.2026) 1. The Commission has expressed its deep concern on the humanitarian situation in Gaza and has made repeated calls for the defence of peace and for the respect of international law and human rights. This was reiterated by the High Representative/Vice-President and other Members of the Commission on several occasions.

The remarks to which the Honourable Member refers were expressed by Executive VicePresident for a Clean, Just and Competitive Transition, as she underscored, in her personal capacity. The Members of the Commission have the right to express their personal opinions, provided they comply with the obligations enshrined in the Treaties and in the Code of Conduct for the Members of the Commission. 2-3.

The statements made by Executive Vice-President for a Clean, Just and Competitive Transition in her personal capacity on the situation in Gaza do not constitute a breach of the ethical obligations to which the Members of the Commission are subjected.
